data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense relies on 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) as a non-probabilistic metric to justify preferring better-corroborated theories. However, Popper's own formal attempt to define verisimilitude logically failed because, without probabilistic assumptions or inductive principles, one cannot rationally assert that a theory with more surviving tests is 'closer to the truth' than a rival; the preference therefore implicitly smuggles in the very inductive assumption (that past survival indicates future reliability or proximity to truth) that the target claims to avoid.
